1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Register two plates using two asymmetric keyholes each. Five widely spaced wires, two windows per plate, quarter-turn rotation, no reflection mismatch, and broad seating tolerances keep the intersection easy to inspect.
1.natural_language: Register both transparent manual plates, then cut the only wire left exposed.

2.label: easy
2.summary: Register three plates using two keyholes each. Six wires, three windows per plate, one required reflection correction, and forgiving quarter-turn alignment add a second transform state.
2.natural_language: Register all three transparent manual plates, then cut the only wire left exposed.

3.label: medium
3.summary: Register four plates on three asymmetric keyholes each. Eight wires, four windows per plate, two reflection corrections, and 45-degree rotation require denser spatial registration.
3.natural_language: Register all four transparent manual plates, then cut the only wire left exposed.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Register the current five transparent plates on three asymmetric pins each, then cut the unique wire shared by all twenty-five apertures.
4.natural_language: Register all five transparent manual plates, then cut the only wire left exposed.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: Register six plates on four asymmetric keyholes each. Eleven densely packed wires, six windows per plate, five reflection corrections, 30-degree rotation, and tight seating tolerances make registration substantially less forgiving.
5.natural_language: Register all six transparent manual plates, then cut the only wire left exposed.

simplified.summary: Drag the active plate, then use binder buttons to rotate, flip, and explicitly seat it on the pins.

full.summary: Drag the active plate directly, right-click it to rotate, Shift-right-click it to flip, and release it on the pins to seat it.
